messages:
Maya Chen: Heads up — the TypeScript sample in sample-app/README.md uses a default import that only works when consumers enable esModuleInterop. I'm seeing reports from a few folks that the quickstart crashes with `TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor` after transpile (ESM projects).

Liam O'Connor: Can you paste the snippet? I think I remember this.

Maya Chen: Sure — this is what's currently in the README:
```ts
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
```

Maya Chen: The package actually exports a named factory: `export function createClient(...)` so the correct usage is:
```ts
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
```

Liam O'Connor: Right. We intentionally avoided a default export to stay compatible with some bundlers and tree-shaking. Also note that turning on `esModuleInterop` would let the default import work, but we shouldn't rely on that in docs.

Sophia Patel: I hit this too when testing the new quickstart on an ESM-next TS template. Error message was confusing for users. Can we patch the README and add a short note about tsconfig?

Maya Chen: Proposed actions: 1) update sample-app README to use the named import; 2) add a one-line note about `esModuleInterop` and why we prefer named exports; 3) include a small troubleshooting FAQ entry. I can open the PR.

Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Make the PR against `devex/docs` branch and ping me for review. Also update the JS snippet to show both cjs and esm variants so copy/paste works. Example:
```js
// CommonJS (Node <14 ESM off)
const { createClient } = require('redwood-inference');
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

// ESM / TS (recommended)
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference';
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
```

doc-bot: New issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/482 — "sample-app README: fix import style to named createClient + note on tsconfig"

Maya Chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/923 — contains README change + FAQ entry. CI kicked off.

ci-bot: build #4278 (docs/pr-923) started — lint/docs checks running.

Sophia Patel: Thanks Maya — can you also add a one-liner to the onboarding checklist so Solutions Engineers who demo the quickstart don't hit this? I can add the checklist item once PR merges. :+1:

Maya Chen: Yep will do. I'll link the checklist update in the PR description and add a short regression test (npm pack + a tiny TS ESM project) to catch this in future.

Liam O'Connor: :eyes: Also maybe add a tiny unit in our sample-app CI that runs `node sample-app/dist/index.js` after building so we catch runtime import issues.

Maya Chen: Added that to the PR as well. CI is green so far for lint. Will merge after one more review.

Sophia Patel: :shipit:

Maya Chen: Merged — changes are live in docs main. Updated the onboarding checklist in the internal Confluence page. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround!

ci-bot: build #4278 (docs/pr-923) completed — all checks passed.
